description:
AUDITED at pinned origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`.

## Current state

`Types::runtime_type_predicate_lists` degrades the entire list axis to `shape_only` whenever any clause has more than one positive signature or any negation (`src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:1373-1375`).

A scratch-instrumented `fz2 interp` census over all 597 checked-in fixture sources completed with zero timeouts. The degrade branch fired 104 times, comprising 8 distinct fixture/type-axis signatures and 4 structural signatures in only three fixtures: `fixtures2/00285_enum_sort_stable.fz`, `fixtures2/behavior/enum_sort.fz`, and `fixtures2/behavior/enum_oracle_smoke.fz`.

Every hit was `list(T) \ []`; there were no multi-positive clauses and no other negation form. Of the 104 calls, 32 projected the genuine non-empty form directly and 72 projected `list(T) | (list(T) \ [])`, whose second clause is redundant.

Subtracting exact `[]` changes only the admitted shape; it removes no cons cell and therefore does not invalidate the positive signature's head predicate. The current blanket rule unnecessarily discards usable head precision, while the corpus does not justify a new TupleShapes-like representation.

## Goal

Exact-empty subtraction preserves the positive list head, and redundant list clauses do not force a coarse runtime question.

## Strategy

1. Add red unit coverage showing `list(T) \ []` projects an exact `NonEmpty` list axis with head `T`, and a mixed descriptor cannot erase another clause's valid head merely because it contains exact-empty subtraction.
2. Normalize/absorb the redundant `list(T) | (list(T) \ [])` form at the list-DNF persistence boundary if that can be done denotationally; keep genuine `list(T) \ []` projectable by classifying exact-empty negations as shape-only.
3. Keep conservative `shape_only` fallback for unmeasured multi-positive clauses and negations that admit cons cells.
4. Add a corpus census/ratchet for degraded list clauses so any future unsupported form is visible, and update `.agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md` to state the precise supported boundary.

## Acceptance

- `list(T) \ []` asks the same head question as `list(T)` while admitting only `NonEmpty`.
- The measured three-fixture population no longer takes the degrade branch.
- Unsupported multi-positive/cons-affecting-negation cases remain soundly shape-only and have unit coverage.
- Full lib, fixture-matrix, CLI, AOT, clippy, and doc gates pass with no warnings.
title: Preserve list-head precision across exact-empty subtraction
